entries.sentence: The NHS says that if a doctor thinks someone has a DVT, they should be referred to hospital within 24 hours for an ultrasound scan.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The scan shows whether blood is flowing normally through the vein.

entries.sentence: A hospital leaflet describes how the D-dimer blood test fits in.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The doctor first estimates the likelihood of a clot using a points score called the Wells score.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: A low score combined with a negative D-dimer is enough to rule out a DVT, and no further tests are needed.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: If the D-dimer is high, a scan is needed.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: If the Wells score is moderate or high, the D-dimer is skipped and the person goes straight to a scan.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: DVT can occur in an arm as well as a leg.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Common features are pain or tenderness, swelling, warmth, redness or discolouration and swollen surface veins, although about half of people with the condition have no symptoms.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS advises calling 999 or going to A&E if leg symptoms come with breathlessness or chest pain.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Blood-thinning medicines (anticoagulants) are the main treatment.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Current NHS advice favours tablets such as rivaroxaban or apixaban, although warfarin is also used.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS says people usually need to take them for at least three months to reduce the risk of another clot.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: A Cambridge hospital leaflet gives more detail on length.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: For a first DVT with no clear cause, three to six months of treatment is usual, depending on the bleeding risk.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: For someone who has had a DVT before, staying on treatment for life is normally recommended.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Blood thinners do not dissolve the clot.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The body absorbs it over time.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The medicine stops it growing and helps prevent new clots.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Clot-busting drugs or surgery are reserved for severe cases.

entries.sentence: All anticoagulants increase the risk of bleeding.

entries.sentence: A Cambridge hospital leaflet lists the signs that need prompt advice from a GP, NHS 111 or, in an emergency, 999: black or bloody stools, blood in the urine, coughing or vomiting blood, severe period bleeding, heavy or persistent nosebleeds and unexplained severe bruising.

entries.sentence: The same leaflet says aspirin and anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen, naproxen or diclofenac should be avoided unless a GP advises otherwise, and that paracetamol is the painkiller generally used alongside anticoagulants.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: It also advises checking with a doctor before taking hormone replacement therapy or the combined contraceptive pill after a clot.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: On travel, a Cambridge leaflet advises delaying flights or long journeys until at least two weeks after starting blood-thinning medicine.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: It adds that aspirin has not been shown to reduce the risk of clots on long journeys, and that anyone who develops leg pain or swelling, chest pain or breathlessness afterwards should seek medical advice.

entries.sentence: The most serious complication is a pulmonary embolism, in which a clot travels to the lungs.

entries.sentence: It can be life-threatening and needs to be treated quickly.

entries.sentence: Post-thrombotic syndrome is the main long-term problem in the leg.

entries.sentence: Compression stockings are a common way to manage the symptoms.

entries.sentence: A UCLH leaflet says they should not be worn until the initial leg swelling has settled, and another hospital leaflet notes that people with circulation or skin problems may not be able to use them.

entries.sentence: A Cambridge hospital leaflet lists these risk factors: a clotting abnormality in the blood, including a family history, pregnancy, obesity, an underlying cancer, a previous DVT, immobility including long-haul flights, contraceptive pills, recent surgery and intravenous drug use.
